cycles.name: Bedrock
focuses: Learn the big lifts properly: squat, hinge and split squat, light and filmed.
Quiet landings, pull-up and dip baselines, and a daily protein habit.

paragraphs: Welcome in, Behnam. This first block is called Bedrock. You've trained for years with your bodyweight, but the bar is new, so these 5 weeks are about learning the big lifts properly. Light on purpose, filmed, done right.

Your padel is already your speed and endurance training. Nobody can out-train 5 or 6 days on court. What the court can't give you is muscle and real strength in your legs, and that is exactly the gym's job. We start with 3 gym days on purpose, so your legs can meet loading without stealing anything from your court play. Day 4 arrives next block.
By the end of Bedrock you'll move weight with confidence, your legs will already feel different, and we'll have real numbers to build everything else on.
outcomes: Squat, hinge and split squat learned and filmed clean
First loaded numbers on the board
Pull-up and dip baselines set in week 1

cycles.name: First Iron
focuses: Novice linear progression on the leg patterns: small steady load jumps, week after week.
The fourth day arrives as an upper day: weighted chin-up and dip work begins.

paragraphs: Next block is called First Iron. The bar starts moving, and then it moves every single week.
You only get one first run at this in your whole lifting life, and we're doing it right. Your fourth day arrives there too.

cycles.name: Structural Build
focuses: Lower-body muscle building: the volume block your legs asked for.
Fueled by the eating habit built in blocks 1 and 2.

cycles.name: Strength Engine
focuses: Heavy lower-body strength: less volume, more weight moving.
Upper strength peaks with weighted pull-up and dip bests.

cycles.name: Power Transfer
focuses: Explosive power at low volume and maximal intent: strength turned into court speed.
Back to three gym days; the extra day goes to your padel.

days.completionMessage: First stones down. Every clean goblet squat rep today is a brick under everything we're building for your legs. Eat well and let the court have you tomorrow.

good: Find an easy steady rhythm
Stay tall and springy on the balls of your feet
bad: Don't hunch over the rope

good: Reach for the ceiling on the twist
Feel the hip of the front leg open up
bad: Don't let the back knee collapse inward

good: Drive the knee over the little toe
Feel a stretch low in the calf and ankle
bad: Don't lift the heel off the floor

good: Push the floor away with your heels
Squeeze the glutes at the top, not the lower back
bad: Don't arch the lower back to go higher

good: Pull yourself down between your knees
Feel the hips and ankles loosen each rep
bad: Don't round the back when you fold down

good: Push the floor away at the top
Feel the shoulder blades spread apart
bad: Don't bend the elbows, this is blades only

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.note: Low box on purpose. The landing is the exercise, so stick it and freeze for 2 seconds. Step down every rep, never jump down.

good: Land soft and freeze like a statue for 2 seconds
Feel the whole foot take the landing, knees over toes
bad: Don't jump down off the box, step down every rep

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.note: First loaded squat, so start with a dumbbell you could do about 15 reps with. Film your last set in weeks 1 and 2 and send it. We add weight when the video looks clean.

good: Push the floor apart and stand up tall
Brace your trunk like you're about to be poked in the stomach
bad: Don't let the dumbbell tip your chest forward

good: Pull the dumbbells to your hips
Feel the shoulder blades pull down and together
bad: Don't shrug the shoulders toward your ears

good: Push the floor away until the elbows lock
Feel the whole body move as one plank
bad: Don't let the hips sag toward the floor

exercises.name: Standing Machine Calf Raise
exercises.note: If the session is running past 50 minutes when you reach this, skip it today. Your calves get their work on day 3 and from the rope.

good: Push the floor away through the big toe
Feel the deep stretch at the bottom before you drive up
bad: Don't bounce out of the bottom

good: Press your lower back into the floor the whole set
Feel the abs hold while the arm and leg move away
bad: Don't let the lower back peel off the floor

days.completionMessage: The hinge is the lift most people get wrong, and you're learning it right from day one. Strong hamstrings are hidden speed on court. Refuel tonight.

good: Find an easy steady rhythm
Stay tall and springy on the balls of your feet
bad: Don't hunch over the rope

good: Push the floor away as you round up
Feel each segment of the spine move one by one
bad: Don't rush, slow beats big

good: Sweep the knees side to side like windshield wipers
Feel the hips rotate, not the lower back
bad: Don't force the knees down with your hands

good: Reach the hand and heel to opposite walls
Feel the trunk stay dead still while the limbs move
bad: Don't let the hips tilt or rotate

good: Tear the band apart to your chest
Feel the muscles between the shoulder blades do the work
bad: Don't shrug up while you pull

good: Walk the hands out to a long plank
Feel the hamstrings stretch on the walk back in
bad: Don't bend the knees more than slightly

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.note: Brace before every rep like you're about to get poked in the stomach. Start light and film your last set in weeks 1 and 2. If your back complains, switch to the cable pull through and message me.

good: Push your hips back to the wall behind you
Feel the hamstrings load like rubber bands stretching
bad: Don't let the back round, the weight stays close and the chest proud

exercises.name: 45° Back Extension
exercises.note: Keep this at RPE 6 for the first two weeks while your body learns the RDL. Push to 7 after that.

good: Lift to a straight line, no higher
Feel the glutes and hamstrings lift you, not the lower back
bad: Don't hyperextend past straight at the top

exercises.name: Strict Pull-Up
exercises.note: First session only: one all-out set of clean reps, filmed. Stop the moment a rep slows down or gets short. That number sets up your weighted pull-ups next block. After it, the last two sets can drop to 4 or 5 reps.

good: Pull your chest to the bar
Feel the lats start the pull before the arms
bad: Don't kip or swing, dead still start every rep

good: Push the pads apart and hold a beat
Feel the side of the hips burn, not the thighs
bad: Don't rock the torso to move more weight

exercises.name: Copenhagen Plank
exercises.note: Knee stays on the bench, not the foot. Week 1: just 2 holds of 10 to 12 seconds each side, easy, and film one. Build to the full 3x15s from week 2. Your groin will thank you on court.

good: Make a straight line from shoulder to top knee
Feel the inner thigh of the top leg hold you up
bad: Don't let the hips drop toward the floor

days.completionMessage: Padel is played one leg at a time, and now you train it that way too. Quiet feet, strong legs. Good week's work, now go eat.

good: Find an easy steady rhythm
Stay tall and springy on the balls of your feet
bad: Don't hunch over the rope

good: Swing the leg like a pendulum, bigger each rep
Feel the hip loosen, not the back arch
bad: Don't force range with momentum

good: Draw a big circle with your knee
Feel the hip move through its whole range
bad: Don't lean the torso to fake the circle

good: Step wide against the band, stay low
Feel the side of the hip work every step
bad: Don't let the knees cave toward each other

good: Sit into one hip, other leg long
Feel the inner thigh stretch on the straight leg
bad: Don't let the bending knee roll inward

good: Take the band over in the widest arc you can
Feel the chest open as the band passes over
bad: Don't bend the elbows to cheat the arc

good: Hop side to side over the line, quick and quiet
Feel the ankles do the bouncing, knees soft
bad: Don't let the feet get loud, loud means sloppy

exercises.name: Dumbbell Split Squat
exercises.note: Session 1 is bodyweight only. Film it. Dumbbells come in once I've cleared the video, same rule as the other big lifts.

good: Drop the back knee straight down to the floor
Feel the front leg do the work, the back leg is a kickstand
bad: Don't let the front knee wobble in and out

exercises.name: Dip
exercises.note: First session only: one all-out set of clean dips, filmed. Stop when a rep slows, sinks too deep or your shoulders shrug. Depth stays comfortable, never forced. This number sets up weighted dips next block.

good: Push the bars away until the elbows lock
Feel the chest and triceps share the push
bad: Don't sink deeper than a comfortable shoulder stretch

good: Row the handle to your belly button
Feel the shoulder blades finish the pull
bad: Don't lean back to yank the weight

good: Push the floor away through the big toe
Feel one calf carry your whole weight
bad: Don't bounce, pause in the bottom stretch

good: Make one straight line from head to feet
Feel the side of the trunk hold you rigid
bad: Don't let the hips sag toward the floor

cards.title: How to pick your weights
cards.body:
The app never gives you a weight. You find it using the RPE number on each exercise. RPE 6 means you could still do 4 more clean reps. RPE 7 means 3 more.

  • New exercise? Start lighter than you think. If the first set feels too easy, go up a little next set.
  • Hit all the reps at or under the target RPE? Add a small jump next week.
  • Missed reps, or the set felt harder than the target? Keep the same weight and repeat it next week.

A rough day where you drop the weight is still a good session. The target is the RPE, not the number on the dumbbell.

cards.title: Your back and shoulder
cards.body:
You told me your lower back and shoulder used to bother you. They're fine now, and this program is built to keep them that way. You don't need to fear any exercise here.

Normal: muscle burn, feeling worked, stiffness the next day. Train through that.

Not normal: sharp pain, pain that shoots down a leg or arm, numbness or tingling, or pain that grows set by set.

  • Mild and fading? Finish the set, write it in your log.
  • Building, or changing how you move? Stop that exercise, do its backup, message me.
  • Sharp, shooting or numb? Stop the session and message me before the next one.

cards.title: Film your top sets
cards.body:
These lifts are new to you and I'm not standing next to you, so video is how I coach you. In weeks 1 and 2, film the last set of your goblet squat, RDL and split squat and send them to me.

Weight goes up on those three only after I've seen the film and cleared it. If the videos stop coming, the weight stops moving. Simple deal.

cards.title: Gym around your padel week
cards.body:
You play 5 or 6 days, so most gym days will also be padel days. That's planned for. Do the gym after padel, or leave 4 to 6 hours between them.

Can't make the gap work, or the day is just too full? Do the short version: the jump or hop drill plus the first big lift, kept easy. Then go home. That still counts.

One more thing. If your calves, achilles or heels feel sore, swap the jump rope for an easy bike or row that day, skip the bottom pause on calf raises, and tell me.

cards.title: The kitchen decides block 3
cards.body:
Block 3 of your plan is the leg-building block you asked for. Here's the honest part: legs don't grow on an accidental diet. You're 70 kg, playing 5 or 6 days and now lifting on top. That burns a lot of food.

  • Protein at every meal. Eggs, chicken, meat, yogurt, whatever works at home.
  • Eat something real before and after training. Never train empty.
  • Log the protein habit in your app every single day.

We'll tune the details in check-ins. But the habit starts now, because block 3 only gets its full size work if your eating is steady by then.

cards.title: The court is your speed coach
cards.body:
You asked for power, speed and endurance. Look at your week: 5 or 6 padel days is already thousands of sprints, lunges and stops. The court trains those better than any gym can. That's why there are no jump programs or leg circuits here yet.

The gym's job is the two things the court can never give you: muscle on your legs and real strength. Build those and every push, first step and stop on court gets a bigger engine behind it.

So please don't add extra jump or sprint sessions on top of this plan. The power block comes in block 5, when there's real strength to turn into speed. And the plan after this whole one goes even harder at leg size. It's all coming. In order.

cards.title: Week 5 is the easy week
cards.body:
Last week of the block: take one set off each big lift and drop every RPE by 1. Same exercises, lighter week.

The easy week is part of the plan. It's what makes First Iron hit harder when the bar starts moving.

And guard that sleep. 7 to 8 hours every night is your biggest recovery weapon, especially once school gets busy.
